name: Background extraction
notes: Placed 108 samples on a 12 x 9 grid, 25 px boxes, 84 accepted and 24 rejected.
Rejected: 24 brighter than the background estimate, 0 on the edge margin, 0 clipped, 0 non-finite.
Every rejected sample is still in the record, with the reason it was rejected.
Thin-plate spline through the 84 accepted samples, smoothing 0.1, per channel and unlinked.
Evaluated on every 8th pixel and interpolated between; measured against direct evaluation at 1000 pixels, worst case 0.00876 of one 8-bit level.

Corrected by subtraction, returning each channel its own model median as the pedestal (R 0.07272, G 0.07564, B 0.06732). The background LEVEL is preserved and only the variation is removed, so the ratio between channels is unchanged and no colour grading happened.
0 pixels came out below zero, which is expected: noise that sat under the model stays under it, and nothing is clamped until the 8-bit step.

name: Colour calibration
notes: Star selection is a brightness cut, not star detection: bright unsaturated pixels are predominantly stars in a star field. Pixels whose neighbourhood is also mostly selected are rejected as extended, which removes a galaxy core but would also remove a star field dense enough to look like one.

hueFidelity.note: preserved by construction; this measures the implementation, not the design

chromaNoise.note: measured on the pixels the mask leaves at k = 1; with the mask wired correctly this cannot grow, so it verifies the mask is on, not that the mask is right

coverageGuard.reason: not evaluable in this chain: an object covering most of the frame is what the background model fits and subtracts, so it never reaches this step as signal. Measured on a frame built with 72.9% coverage, only 115 pixels survived as extended. The guard is empty by construction, not missing a test case.

name: Quantise to 8-bit
notes: Dithered by plus or minus 0.5 of one level before rounding, from a fixed seed (20260906), so the result is reproducible from the same file.
0 values below black and 0 above white were clamped here, out of 589824.
